chunks: And from him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said:
He said: 'What do people say regarding having intercourse with women from their rears?' I said to him: 'It has reached me that the People of the Book do not see anything wrong with that.'
He said: 'Indeed, the Jews used to say: When a man comes to a woman from behind, the child is born squint-eyed.'
So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: 'Your wives are a tilth for you; so come to your tilth as you wish.'
He said: 'From the front and from the rear, in contrast to the statement of the Jews, and it did not mean specifically in their rears.'

And this report, which we have presented earlier, does not contradict our earlier statement regarding the permissibility of this matter, because it only included that the interpretation of the verse is as mentioned, and it does not say that whoever performs the specific act has committed a prohibition. And that which reveals the permissibility of that is also what was narrated:

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْكِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on having intercourse with women from behind according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the phrase 'as you wish' in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:223 refers to the variety of sexual positions rather than restricting the act to the front, thereby refuting the Jewish belief that rear-entry intercourse causes squint-eyed offspring. This narration, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes the permissibility of intercourse from behind as a general rule rather than a specific exception, highlighting the Shia scholarly approach to reconciling Quranic exegesis with pre-Islamic cultural beliefs.
